recipes.name: 3BC (Best Baked Bean Casserole)
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can baked beans (such as Bush's Original®)

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Melt butter in a large skillet over low heat. Add onion and cook until soft and translucent, 10 to 15 minutes. Transfer to a 2-quart casserole dish and set aside. Cook bacon in the same skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon on a paper towel-lined plate. Cut bacon into bite-sized pieces and set aside.

Combine baked beans, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard in the casserole dish. Stir in 2/3 cooked bacon and 1/4 brown sugar until mixture is combined. Top bean mixture with remaining bacon and sprinkle with remaining brown sugar.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot and bubbly, about 45 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Used this as a base recipe and really enjoyed it. I was asked to make 20 servings of baked beans for a child's party. I used 2 (55 oz each) cans and 1 (28 oz) can of Bush's Original baked beans, 4 packages of Oscar Meyer bacon crumbles (the ones in the bag near the croutons, salad dressing, etc.), 1 large onion (minced fine), 1 1/2 cups of brown sugar (which was plenty), 3 1/2 Tbsp of ketchup, 1 1/2 Tbsp of mustard, 1 3/4 Tbsp of Worcestershire and added 1 1/2 - 2 tsps. of Liquid Smoke along with 1 tsp of garlic powder and 1 tsp of black pepper. Cooked in the slow cooker on low for 4 1/2 hours then switched to warm to keep them hot for the party. Everyone loved them. I will definitely make these again for family gatherings!

I modified this recipe quite a bit. It served about 13 people as a side dish. It came out fabulous. My boyfriend who does not like baked beans and never has, LOVED them. He put them in a solo cup and poured them into his mouth because he liked them so much haha! I also used B&M original beans.


• 2 tablespoon butter
• 1 yellow onion, finely diced
• 1 pound bacon
• 2 (28 ounce) can baked beans 
• 4 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
• 2 tablespoon ketchup
• 2 teaspoon prepared deli mustard
• 2/3 cup brown sugar, divided

Directions

1. Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
2. Cook bacon in a skillet or bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes. Allow to cool and chop into pieces about the size of a dime. 
3. Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add chopped onions and sauté until soft.
4. Add 2 cans of beans to the skillet and stir until hot.
5. Add Worcestershire sauce, ketchup and mustard. Stir until evenly blended.
6. Measure out 2/3 cup of brown sugar, packed. Break apart with a fork before adding to the skillet. Once broken up, add to the skillet and stir until the brown sugar is completely melted. 
7. Pour into a baking dish. Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.

Pretty good recipe for baked beans that is easy to make and adjust to taste preference. I followed the recipe as written, but had to make some adjustments, hence the 3 star rating. I discovered that canned baked beans contains brown sugar and tasted pretty sweet as is. So, I cut way back on the brown sugar...stirred in about 1/8 cup and topped the bacon with just a tiny bit more brown sugar. I also suggest watching your bake time. These were not extra runny/soupy at all. I would remove them earlier than 45 minutes to prevent them from drying out (used my cast iron skillet so maybe that's why I was losing so much liquid, so to speak). This will be a go to and repeat here, but with changes noted above. Thanks for the recipe.

I tasted the bean mixture after adding the 1/4 cup brown sugar, and it was already very, very sweet. I looked at the label on the can, and brown sugar is listed as the fourth ingredient, so my gut was telling me that another 3/4 cup brown sugar on top of the casserole would ruin this. I used a little less than 1/4 cup sprinkled on top of the bacon, and these beans still are really sweet (probably will cut back to 1/8 cup mixed into the bean mixture in the future). I took out of the oven at 30 min because they were cooked perfectly for us. We like them cold as well as hot, so a consistency just a little runny makes great leftovers for the next day. All in all, not a bad recipe and not a lot of work either.

So based on many reviews I doubled the recipe and as I don't care for too sweet stuff I elected to go with 1/4 brown sugar total even when I doubled the ingredients and I think this turned out perfect. Many compliments at dinner table too. I put it all in a slow cooker for 4 hours on low and will definitely make again.

Added 2 T maple syrup, followed all other direction - very good. Was in rush 2nd time to make, so I cooked on stove top, medium heat, using automatic stir things from drugstore - awesome and fast. Just take off once sugars thicken. This is a keeper
Doubled the recipe and added a can of butter beans. Didn't double the brown sugar. Yum

I doubled the batch. I put it in my crock pot for Christmas day, then baked at the end without the extra brown sugar (since I read it can be too sweet). It was awesome with ham, and with all the left overs days later!
Received compliments from two very good cooks. Easy to make! I doubled the recipe and cooked it covered in a dutch oven.

These baked beans were great. I reduced the amount of brown sugar to 1/4 cup, and that was perfect for us. Served them at a summer cookout party along with grilled hot dogs, potato salad, and watermelon, and it was the perfect side to go along with what we were having. There wasn't a single bean left after our party. I would definitely make these again and would probably double the recipe because they were popular.
This was too sweet for my taste. A cup of brown sugar in this recipe is at least 1/2 cup too much. I am going to keep looking for another recipe or modify this one next time.
My family asks for these every time we have a BBQ. Top with cheddar cheese for an added treat.
I made this last night and it was delicious. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing this recipe.
This turned out so good, and I even used a cheap can of baked beans. We ate this as a meal and my family all went back for seconds.
we used hickory brown sugar beans, it was so good it disappeared within minutes, wish i had made more.
These beans were AMAZING!!! My whole family enjoyed them, which is a miracle. Another bonus is how eeaasssy they are to make. A win win!!
